summary: A 60-foot steel fire tower was erected at Muirkirk in 1926 and had a forest guard by 1930; the association lists it as gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association. No source read describes the site today.

staffing.status: forest guard stationed at the tower, per a state forestry report for FY 1930

events.note: State forestry officials sought a site for a fire watch tower in Prince Georges County; the newspaper plan put the height at 60 feet near the railroad lines
A 60-foot steel tower erected and ready for service, per the state's FY 1930 report
Combined workshop and garage built at the Muirkirk tower in late 1929
Forest guard stationed at the tower; the watchman joined him in the shop on damp or rainy days

evidence.supports: July 1925 state forestry officials seeking a tower site in Prince Georges County
evidence.quote: State forestry officials are seeking a site for the location of a fire watch tower in Prince Georges County, where numerous fires recently damaged valuable timber.

evidence.supports: planned tower near the Baltimore-Washington railroad lines, 60 feet high
evidence.quote: The tower will be erected near the Baltimore-Washington railroad lines and will be 60 feet high.

evidence.supports: 1926 60-foot steel tower erected and ready for service
evidence.quote: A 60-foot steel tower was erected and ready for service.

evidence.supports: late 1929 workshop and garage built at the tower
evidence.quote: Late in 1929 a combined workshop and garage was built at the Muirkirk Forest Fire Tower

evidence.supports: forest guard stationed at the tower in 1930
evidence.quote: The forest guard stationed at the tower spent his time, while waiting for fire calls, working in the shop.

evidence.supports: 1930 shop work: fire tool repairs, sign posts, tool boxes for the wardens
evidence.quote: repair of damaged fire tools, preparation of sign posts and sign backs for mounting, construction of special fire tool boxes for the forest wardens

evidence.supports: association lists the Muirkirk tower as gone
Burtonsville tower built in 1926, later moved to Columbia Pike, proposed for demolition
evidence.quote: the University owned Burtonsville Fire Tower, which was built in 1926, but was later moved to a site along Columbia Pike (US Route 29), was proposed to be demolished.

sources.title: Maryland's Forest Fire Lookout Towers Poster

notes_for_editor: The 1926 build date and the 1929-1930 workshop and guard come from one association page quoting a state forestry report for FY 1930; they are solid but secondhand. The status 'gone' rests on the association list alone. A search summary said the Muirkirk tower was moved to Burtonsville in 1932, and that a DNR poster gives 2014 demolition details, but the poster PDF returned 404 and the summary was not a page I could read, so the 1932 move is not in the story and the Burtonsville link is marked unconfirmed. The association lists Muirkirk and Burtonsville as separate Gone entries. Nothing read describes the Muirkirk site today. The brief's 18.3 m height matches the 60-foot figure. Web searches used: 2 (cap 2). Pages read: about 6.
